analogies: The difference between a reference librarian and a personal assistant — one answers questions, the other gets things done.
definition: Agentic describes an AI system that pursues a goal on its own: it breaks the goal into steps, uses tools to take actions, looks at the results, and adjusts its plan. A chatbot answers your question and stops. An agentic system keeps working until the job is done — searching the web, checking your calendar, writing the email, booking the flight — more like hiring someone to handle a task than asking someone for advice.

edges.label: runs on
edges.note: The goal → plan → act → observe cycle is the engine behind agentic behavior.

edges.label: needs a
edges.note: Agentic behavior needs a harness — the model on its own can't touch tools.

edges.label: kept safe by
edges.note: An AI that can act in the world needs rules about what it's allowed to touch.

example.body: You tell it: "Book me a flight to Chicago under $400 for next Friday." An agentic system searches flight options, checks your calendar for conflicts, compares prices, picks one, and books it — then reports back. You didn't answer five follow-up questions; you gave a goal and got a result. If the first option sells out, it tries the next one instead of giving up.
example.title: Booking a flight while you make lunch

footnotes.body: Agentic behavior is usually implemented as a loop — the agentic loop: the model plans, calls tools (via function calling / tool use), observes the tool outputs, and repeats. The 'agency' comes from the harness around the model (tools, memory, permissions), not from the model weights alone. There is no bright line where a system becomes 'agentic'; it is a spectrum from single tool calls to long autonomous runs.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Agentic
tagline: When an AI doesn't just answer — it plans, acts, and adjusts to reach a goal.
whyItMatters: This is the shift from AI as a smarter search box to AI as a coworker that does things. It unlocks real usefulness — software that completes multi-step jobs while you're away — but it also raises the stakes: a system that acts can also act wrongly, which is why permissions and guardrails matter as much as capability.
